'''Merana Ambrey''' is an [[Aes Sedai]] of the [[Gray Ajah]].{{ref|{{twotc}}, Merana Ambrey}} She is notable for being the one initially put in charge of the [[Salidar Embassy to the Dragon Reborn]].

== Appearance and Personality==
Merana is on the slim side of a medium build, with dark hair and hazel eyes.{{ref/book|7|34}}{{ref/book|6|43}} She is about 5'4 tall.

==Strength and Abilities==
Merana is [[Strength in the One Power among Aes Sedai|strong]] for an Aes Sedai, with a [[One Power]] level of {{opsl|23}}. 

She is above the stated minimum strength to be able to [[Traveling|Travel]].

==History==
She is from [[Andor]], from [[Caemlyn]].

Merana is 111 years old. She was born in [[Caemlyn]] in {{ne|889}} and went to the [[White Tower]] in {{ne|907}}. After spending five years as a [[novice]] and six years as [[Accepted]], she was raised to the [[shawl]] in {{ne|918}}.

In {{ne|961}}, Merana was responsible for negotiating the [[Fifth Treaty of Falme]] for the peaceful disposition of [[Almoth Plain]] between [[Arad Doman]] and [[Tarabon]]. Unfortunately it failed almost immediately.{{ref/book|6|43}} She was also part of the futile Gray Ajah effort to make the Grand Coalition last after the Aiel War.

Her [[Warder]], [[Basan]], was killed before the [[Aiel War]] and she has not bonded another.

==Activities==
She is allied to the [[Salidar Aes Sedai]].

===Ambassador===
Although Merana was in charge of the [[Salidar Embassy to the Dragon Reborn]] sent to [[Caemlyn]], she had insecurities about her position due to the high number of strong sisters in the group. [[Rafela Cindal]], [[Faeldrin Harella]] and [[Masuri Sokawa]] were all stronger than her, with [[Seonid Traighan]] being her equal.{{ref/book|6|p}}{{ref/book|6|41}} That mattered less because she had been granted authority over them, although the imbalance still made her uneasy. More troubling was the later arrival of [[Verin Mathwin]] and [[Alanna Mosvani]], both of whom were not under orders to respect her assigned authority as they were not of the Salidar faction. Both were the same strength as she, but Verin was her superior due to her age.{{ref/book|6|43}} Later still, the arrival of [[Bera Harkin]] and [[Kiruna Nachiman]] destroyed her authority entirely. Both were very strong in the Power and enough so that she should defer to them under regular circumstances. What was more, they had been assigned to approach the Dragon Reborn on behalf of the Rebels at a time prior to her own orders, which could conceivably supersede her position. 

Although initially instructed to shepherd the Two Rivers girls to Salidar, Merana was allowed to accompany them to [[Cairhien]] after [[Rand al'Thor]] fled [[Andor]] as the others might need her Gray skills as a negotiator.{{ref/book|6|43}}

=== Dumai's Wells ===
Merana joined the Battle at [[Dumai's Wells]] with [[Perrin]]'s forces, but she was forced to swear fealty to Rand after the battle.{{ref/book|6|55}}

=== Fealty to Rand ===
After returning to Cairhien, in the Sun Palace Merana accepts to be used as a servant by Rand to convince some of the [[Aiel]] [[clan chief]]s that he is not an Aes Sedai puppet.{{ref/book|7|18}}

Some time after [[Cadsuane Melaidhrin]] arrives in Cairhien she takes Merana away and questions her heavily on the events that have transpired lately.{{ref/book|7|19}} However, Merana gathers the courage to confront Cadsuane directly and asks her about her intentions to the Lord Dragon. Merana also tells Cadsuane that she will help and protect him with the aid of the other sworn sisters.

Some time after Rand, as the [[Coramoor]], meets with [[Harine din Togara Two Winds]], as the Extraordinary Embassador from the Mistress of Ships of the [[Atha'an Miere|Atha'an Miere;]] after the meeting he leaves Merana Ambrey and [[Rafela Cindal]] to negotiate his Bargain with Harine{{ref/book|7|34}}.

Rand initially isn't too pleased with the two Aes Sedai over the final points of the Bargain, causing Merana to strongly chastise him for his unfair expectations of the sisters, especially as he left when they had the upper hand. His ta'veren nature had caused Harine to make concessions, and after Rand left, Harine accused Merana and Rafela of using the One Power to trick her. Merana and others are shocked at her outburst, but Rand realizes this also happened due to his ta'veren nature twisting probability. Thus, Rand accepts this and apologizes to Merana and Rafela, while realizing the political advantages that were made in the bargain.{{ref/book|8|27}}

In Far Madding Rand orders to Alanna to pick up Merana and some of the other sworn Aes Sedai from Salidar in Cairhien, to go negotiate with the Tairiens rebels.{{ref/book|9|32}} Merana is spotted by the [[Rebel Aes Sedai|Rebel]] [[Amyrlin Seat]]'s [[Eyes-and-ears]] in Tear, possibly mediating a negotiation between the [[Steward of the Dragon]] High Lord [[Darlin Sisnera]], and the leaders of the rebel forces, High Lord [[Tedosian]] and High Lady [[Estanda]].{{ref/book|10|18}}

Merana finally draws an agreement with the rebel [[High Lords of Tear]]. The terms are that the rebels will disperse in return for Darlin being made king.{{ref/book|11|21}}

As with many Aes Sedai sworn to Rand, Merana probably fought the [[Last Battle]] on the slopes of [[Thakan'dar]].{{ref/book|14|34}} She is not mentioned and likely survived.

== Viewing ==
[[Min Farshaw]] sees her in the palm of Rand's hand. This indicates she will keep her oath and can be trusted by Rand.{{ref/book|7|34}} Because it is not stated otherwise it can also be presumed that she survives.
